s='''# Independent ordinary proof for MathDB 377665

Constructed before reading FULLCANDIDATE.md. No mathematical computation or formal tool was used.

Let G be a finitely generated abelian group, written additively. An avoiding coloring c:G -> F2 obeys c(x)+c(y)=1 whenever x != y and x+y belongs to U. Saturated means avoidable and inclusion-maximal among ALL avoidable subsets of G. Assume U intersect 2G is empty.

For u in U define R_u(x)=u-x. It has no fixed point: a fixed point would give u=2x. Thus c(R_u(x))=c(x)+1 for every x, without exception. For a finite ordered list u_1,...,u_k, compose in chronological order R_{u_k} ... R_{u_1}. Induction gives (-1)^k x + A, where A=sum_{j=1}^k (-1)^{k-j}u_j. If k is odd and sum q(u_j)=0 in V=G/2G, then q(A)=0 as signs agree modulo 2. Hence A=2x for some x. At this x the composite returns x, but its color changes k times, contradiction. Each step has distinct endpoints because its label is outside 2G. Repeated labels, revisited vertices, non-simple closed walks and nonunique halves from 2-torsion cause no problem: the color toggles at every step. The list is finite even if U is infinite.

Consequently every finite list in q(U) with zero sum has even length. Put W=span_F2(q(U)). Define f(sum_{j=1}^k q(u_j))=k mod 2, including the empty sum. Two presentations concatenate to a zero relation, so their lengths have equal parity. Concatenation also proves additivity; scalar linearity over F2 follows. In particular f(q(u))=1. This uses only finite-support linear combinations, not finite generation of U.

The finitely generated group G has finite-dimensional V: images of any finite generating list span it. Choose a basis of W, extend to a basis of V by successively adjoining vectors outside the current span, and give all added basis vectors value 0. This defines a linear extension F:V -> F2. Let phi=F composed with q. Then U is contained in H={g:phi(g)=1}. H is avoidable by coloring phi: same-color sums have phi-value 0. Maximality of U among all avoidable subsets gives U=H.

Nonemptiness must be paid before claiming phi nonzero. The singleton {0} is avoidable: enumerate G using a fixed finite generating list, words in integer exponents ordered by increasing total absolute exponent and then a finite tie order, and give each element its first index. For each two-element orbit {x,-x} give the earlier element color 0 and the other color 1. Give singleton orbits color 0. If distinct x,y sum to 0, they lie in one two-element orbit and have opposite colors. Thus the empty set cannot be saturated. A nonempty U then forces phi nonzero. No unproved infinite orbit-choice assertion is used. For |G|>=2, if both parts must be nonempty and the coloring is constant, all negation orbits are singleton and any splitting off of one element still avoids {0}. For the trivial group, the graph-coloring convention allows empty color classes, {0} is avoidable, and necessity is vacuous. Under a strict two-nonempty-block convention the trivial group admits no avoidable set at all, so again there is no saturated U to consider. No unconditional existence theorem for strict partitions on the trivial group is claimed.

Coordinates: write G as a finite direct sum of odd-order cyclic factors and H_i factors, each infinite cyclic or even-order cyclic (the source displays 2-power cyclic factors; either formulation has the same parity coordinates). Doubling is onto each odd factor, so homomorphisms to F2 vanish there. On Z or Z/(2^e Z), e>=1, a homomorphism has the form x_i -> a_i(x_i mod 2). Therefore phi(x)=sum_i a_i x_i mod 2. Nonzero phi means some a_i=1, and U is exactly the displayed level-one solution set. In Theorem 3's notation the parity dimension is m2+m3+r; the odd-factor contribution is zero. Finite groups, free rank zero, no torsion and mixed groups are all included. When V=0 (G=2G, including all finite odd-order groups and the trivial group), U would have to be empty, which is not saturated under the coloring convention, so the implication has no instances. No nonzero coefficient vector in dimension zero is invented.

Separate converse warning: in an elementary abelian 2-group every distinct pair has nonzero sum, so adding 0 never affects avoidability. For nonzero phi, H is avoidable but H union {0} is also avoidable, hence H is NOT saturated. For G=Z/2 this is immediate from the partition into its two singleton elements. This refutes the preceding blanket sufficiency sentence but does not refute the necessity implication: in exponent two there are no saturated even-free sets. More generally H is saturated if G is not of exponent two: its sum graph is complete bipartite on the phi fibers, hence an avoiding coloring is that partition up to swapping. For e != 0 with phi(e)=0, the distinct same-color pair 0,e forbids adding e. For e=0 choose x with 2x !=0; then x,-x are distinct and have the same phi-value, forbidding addition of 0. This extra observation is separate, uncredited and unnecessary for necessity.

Adversarial checks: using homogeneous coloring for U would be false; only the enlarged H has a homomorphic coloring. Inclusion in H alone would not finish the target; maximality supplies equality. Distinct summands exclude loops only; odd U makes every reflection step a genuine edge. There is no bound on |U| and no transfer from finite groups. No division by 2 is made outside 2G and no uniqueness of a half is assumed.
'''
